traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are implemented and verified. The valid-annotation-format rule now supports both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern) and flat (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern) configuration options with corresponding example fields. Regex patterns are validated at configuration time with clear, stable error messages; invalid patterns are reported via invalidRuleConfiguration and the rule safely falls back to default patterns, preserving backward compatibility and auto-fix behavior. JSON Schema for the options is defined in getRuleSchema and used in rule meta, following ESLint best practices. Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts explicitly cover all listed requirements (configurable patterns, examples in messages, invalid regex handling, nested vs flat precedence, and fallback behavior), and the full Jest test suite passes. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md provides clear nested and flat configuration examples and explains invalid configuration behavior, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion and aligning with the existing valid-story-reference configuration model. No discrepancies between the story and the implementation were found.
